Course Description: 
This course is designed to provide Direct Second Year Engineering students with essential knowledge in 
basic mathematics and foundational communication skills necessary for academic and professional 
success. The mathematics component strengthens core concepts such as algebra, trigonometry, and 
calculus, forming the basis for advanced engineering subjects. The communication component focuses on 
enhancing students’ proficiency in written and oral communication, including resume writing, 
professional correspondence, and presentation skills. The course aims to bridge educational gaps and 
prepare students for effective participation in engineering academics and industry environments. 
Course Learning Objectives: 
1. To bridge the gap in fundamental mathematics essential for core engineering subjects. 
2. To develop clear and effective communication skills in academic and professional contexts. 
3. To enhance problem-solving abilities and interpersonal communication relevant to industry 
expectations.

Course Contents: 
Unit: 1 
 
Fundamental Concepts of Engineering Mathematics (7 hours) 
• 
Algebraic operations: Simplification, Factorization, Surds and Indices 
• 
Introduction to logarithms and their properties 
• 
Functions and Graphs: Concept of function, domain and range, standard curves 
• 
Partial Fraction, Vector Algebra  
• 
Trigonometry review: Basic identities, solution of triangles, applications 
07 Hrs. 
Unit: 2 
 
Calculus Essentials and Applications  
• 
Limits and continuity (basic concepts and standard problems) 
• 
Differentiation: Rules, standard derivatives, chain rule 
• 
Applications of derivatives: Rate of change, maxima and minima, curve sketching 
• 
Introduction to integration and simple problems of area under curves 
• 
Partial Derivatives 
08 Hrs. 

Page 2 of 2 
 
Unit: 3 
 
Communication for Academic and Professional Success 
• 
Basics of effective communication: Verbal, Non-verbal, and Written 
• 
Listening skills and note-taking techniques 
• 
Formal letter and email writing (for internship, placement, official requests) 
• 
Resume and cover letter writing 
07 Hrs. 
Unit: 4 
 
Oral Communication and Presentation Skills  
• 
Group discussions and interpersonal skills 
• 
Public speaking: Structure, clarity, and confidence 
• 
Presentation strategies: Use of visual aids, audience engagement 
• 
Interview skills: Mock interviews, body language, and etiquette 
08 Hrs.

2. "Engineering Mathematics" by H.K. Dass and Er. Rajnish Verma, S. Chand Publishing 
3. “A Textbook of Engineering Mathematics” by N.P. Bali and Manish Goyal, Laxmi Publications 
4. “Differential Calculus & Integral Calculus” by Shanti Narayan and P.K. Mittal, S. Chand Publishing 
 
Communication Skills: 
1. "Technical Communication" by Meenakshi Raman & Sangeeta Sharma, Oxford University Press
